sentence: This project coordinates and supports educational activities across cancer biology, prevention, and care.
This project studies how a fusion transcript made from two adjacent genes may make lung adenocarcinoma more aggressive in some patients.
This project offers assays that measure DNA damage and epigenetic changes linked to aging.
This project studies a type of T cell in cord blood to understand how infants respond to infections.
This project tries to find out why some people with type 1 diabetes get coronary artery disease while others resist it.
This project studies how latent HIV reservoirs are formed and maintained.
This project studies how endothelial cells in mouse skin communicate with epithelial stem cells during the hair cycle.
This project supports pilot research projects on topics such as cancer prevention, brain metastasis, and cancer immunotherapy.
This project studies how a molecular machine called condensin controls genes.
This project holds a meeting about understanding and treating congenital diseases with cell and gene therapy.
This project looks at gene expression in brain regions of people who died by suicide to find biological causes.
This project studies whether unstable regulatory T cells can show how active lupus is and how they drive harmful immune responses.
This project builds a tool that predicts which cancer patients are at higher risk of drug-induced cardiovascular decline.
This project studies immune mechanisms that drive long-term autoimmunity in autoimmune endocrinopathies, including thyroiditis and type 1 diabetes.
This project provides flow cytometry technology and expert help for cancer researchers.
This project studies how the metabolism of gut protists affects the bacteria that share the human gut.
This project tests drugs in genetically heterogeneous mice to see whether they increase healthy lifespan.
This project searches for genetic risk factors of central serous chorioretinopathy and choroidal thickening.
This project studies early changes in cholinergic signaling in the prefrontal cortex of males and females with a Parkinson's-linked mutation.
This project builds an AI tool that reads scanned histopathology slides to predict a gene mutation in breast cancer patients.
